title: Bulgarian — BDS 1596:1973 / UN 1977
authority: Bulgarian State Standard BDS 1596:1973 'Transliteration of Bulgarian words with Latin characters' (effective 1 Jan 1975); Council of Orthography and Transcription of Geographical Names, Sofia (1972); UN resolution III/10 (1977)
description: Slavic scientific-style system with diacritics (ž č š št, ǎ for Ъ, j for Й and Ь, ju/ja, c for Ц), the Bulgarian national standard and UN system for geographical names until the 2009 Transliteration Act. Useful for matching older documents (Jordan, Cvetan, Koljo).
notes: The primary text of BDS 1596:1973 was not available. The letters follow the UN WGRS report for the 1972 Sofia system approved by the UN in 1977 (ž j c č š št ǎ j ju ja, х→h), which Wikipedia identifies with BDS 1596:1973 and ISO/R 9:1968.
Ъ is ǎ (U+01CE, a with caron) as printed by the UN WGRS; the scientific transliteration and some sources use ă (U+0103).

Ivanov, Skordev and Dobrev (2009) describe 'diacritics-free versions' of BDS 1596:1973 with й→j, ц→c, ь→j, ю→ju, я→ja; Bulgaria's 2012 UN paper says the 1999 ID-document table was BDS 1596:73 with only Й/Ю/Я changed, implying a digraph variant (zh, ch, sh, sht, ъ→a). That variant is not encoded here.
The interscript map un-bul-Cyrl-Latn-1977 uses yu/ya for ю/я; this contradicts the UN WGRS report (ju/ja), which is followed here.
ьо → jo and йо → jo follow from the letter table; there is no -ия exception (Мария → Marija).
